content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I'm trying to enable communication between Python and a [product_name] [version_no] on Ubuntu Linux. I've spent a couple of weeks using a Python wrapper ([url]), but my Python skills aren't strong enough to get it working. Has anyone had success with this? Apologies for any language mistakes. [user_name] [user_name] Tech School Barcelona
Hi, here is an example for Python 2.7. You can start it from the IDLE or with ./[product_name].py. [user_name]
Thanks [user_name]! I'll give it a try tomorrow.
Success! It is working now! Thank you [user_name].

Hi everyone, I've made some changes to the Python libraries thanks to [user_name] using libnodave. Does anyone know how to use these functions: daveStop, daveStart, daveReadPLCTime, daveSetPLCTime, daveSetPLCTimeToSystime? I can't get them to work. [user_name] [user_name] Tech School Barcelona

Hi, those functions aren't compatible with [product_name]. To start or stop the [product_name], you can send control codes directly. Here's a simple example: #!/usr/bin/python import socket from Tkinter import * [product_name]_IP = "192.168.2.50" Port = 10001 def [product_name]_Start(): s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) s.connect(([product_name]_IP, Port)) s.send('\x55\x18\x18\xAA') s.close() def [product_name]_Stop(): s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) s.connect(([product_name]_IP, Port)) s.send('\x55\x12\x12\xAA') s.close() master=Tk() b=Button(master, text='[product_name] Run', command=[product_name]_Start) b.pack() c=Button(master, text='[product_name] Stop', command=[product_name]_Stop) c.pack() master.mainloop() [user_name]

Thanks for this example with libnodave, but I'm encountering an issue: Trying to connect... - Port Handle OK. - Dave Interface Handle : 5440888 - Init Adapter OK. - Dave Connection: 5450912 - Result: -1 Why is the result -1? I appreciate your help.
Hello, Could you help me with other [product_name] [version_no] commands or possibly HTML if available? Thank you [user_name]
Hi [user_name], why did you write your question in French? The whole thread is in English. However, here's an attempt at a translation. Best regards

Hello, Sorry, my English is not very good. I'd like to read the input/output values of the [product_name] [version_no] via port 10001 using a Python socket, similar to [user_name]'s example below. I found some additional command sequences /X55, X19, X19, XAA to read data, but I am unable to receive the data. Thank you! Example: import socket from Tkinter import * [product_name]_IP = "192.168.2.50" Port = 10001 def [product_name]_Start(): s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) s.connect(([product_name]_IP, Port)) s.send('\x55\x18\x18\xAA') s.close() def [product_name]_Stop(): s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) s.connect(([product_name]_IP, Port)) s.send('\x55\x12\x12\xAA') s.close()
Hi [user_name], this is my final (poor) attempt at a translation for you. Maybe your English isn't great, but my French is much worse. I hope you find the answer you're looking for. Regards

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working on establishing communication between a [product_name] [version_no] and Python using libnodave on Linux systems. Basic functionality is confirmed, but advanced functions such as starting, stopping, or managing PLC time do not operate due to compatibility limitations. Alternative control code approaches via sockets are shared, and queries about error codes and unreliability in the documentation suggest gaps in integration guidance and API support.
